title: TESS eclipse times from 2018 to 2026 show that TYC 9179-1083-1 is an eccentric 10.29-day binary with a 1-solar-mass third star on a 5.9-year orbit at 55 degrees that can cause its deepening eclipses
abstract: A prior campaign study found that both eclipses of the TESS binary TIC 300560295 (TYC 9179-1083-1) become deeper from 2018 to 2026, and suggested a third body. We measured the time, depth and width of every eclipse in 42 TESS 2-min sectors (2018-2026) and fitted dynamical models. The period is 10.2944 d, not the catalogue value of 20.5888 d: the two deep catalogue eclipses are one primary eclipse, and a shallow secondary eclipse occurs at phase 0.813 (e = 0.51). Primary depths are 2.51, 3.01, 3.85 and 4.43 percent and secondary depths 0.19, 0.35, 0.76 and 1.06 percent in four seasons. The primary times change by about 70 min. A precessing inner orbit alone gives chi2 = 6,365 for 161 data; a light-travel-time orbit lowers it to 479, with an outer period of 2,129 d; outer periods of 2,700 d or more give chi2 >= 648. With primary times only, reduced chi2 is about 1.0. A three-body N-body model fits 86 primary and 67 secondary times (chi2 = 76.3 and 73.1) with an outer period of 2,147 +- 13 d, outer e = 0.065, a tertiary of 1.03 +- 0.02 solar masses (for assumed inner masses 1.05 + 0.23) and a mutual inclination of 55.1 +- 1.2 degrees (54.7-55.4 for other inner masses). The model increases the inner inclination and eccentricity in the observed directions, so the third star can cause the deepening; its inclination change is 1.6-1.9 times larger than the light-curve value, and it does not reproduce the light-curve change of the periastron angle. The model has Kozai-Lidov cycles of about 1,090 years and predicts an eclipse window from about 2003-2015 to 2130-2143. Gaia DR3 (RUWE 8.4, acceleration solution) agrees with an unresolved 5.9-year orbit. Limitations: grazing eclipses leave the radius ratio and absolute inclination undetermined, inner masses are assumed, there is no photodynamical fit, and only TESS data are used. We give eclipse-time forecasts for 2026-2030.

display.caption: TESS data folded at the catalogue period 20.5888 d show two copies of one primary eclipse and of one shallow secondary eclipse; the true period is 10.2944 d. Both eclipses become deeper from 2018 to 2026.
Eclipse times relative to a linear ephemeris and the best three-body model (outer period 2,147 d, tertiary 1.03 solar masses, mutual inclination 55 degrees). Primary residual rms 0.38 min.
Best three-body model over 8,000 years: eclipses occur only in short windows; the present window started near 2003-2015; Kozai-Lidov cycles change the inner e from 0.42 to 0.71.
